matches.title: Laval vs Nantes
matches.description: Watch Laval vs Nantes highlights and goals from Ligue 2 on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on August 14, 2026. Tension was palpable as Laval welcomed Nantes for a highly anticipated showdown in Ligue 2 . Both teams entered the pitch with everything to play for, setting the stage for a match that would keep fans on the edge of their seats until the very end. Early Exchanges and the Opening Breakthrough On August 14, 2026, the contest began with high energy but was quickly interrupted by physical concerns for both sides. As early as the 12th minute, Laval was forced into a substitution when Francis Coquelin had to make way for Ethan Clavreul . Shortly after, Wilitty Younoussa was also replaced by Louis Leroux . Despite these forced adjustments, the home side remained focused on their offensive objectives. The persistence paid off in the 17th minute. The newly introduced Ethan Clavreul made an immediate impact, providing a clinical assist for Trevis Dago , who found the back of the net to put Laval ahead. The goal galvanized the home crowd, but Nantes showed resilience as they searched for a response before the break. Nantes Responds and Tactical Shifts As the first half drew to a close, Nantes ramped up their pressure. In the 44th minute, Bahereba Guirassy struck a crucial equalizer, clinical finishing ensuring that both teams went into the tunnel level at the break. The goal shifted the momentum, and the second half became a tactical chess match as both managers turned to their benches to find a winning edge. In the second half, fresh legs were introduced, including Mathieu Cafaro for the visitors and Mathis Houdayer for the hosts. While the game remained tightly contested with defensive discipline on both sides, the intensity never wavered. As the clock ticked toward ninety minutes, a yellow card for Julien Maggiotti signaled the rising stakes and desperation in the final stages. Stoppage-Time Drama Just when it appeared the points would be shared, the match reached a dramatic climax in stoppage time. In the 95th minute, Mathis Houdayer capitalized on a late opportunity to score a sensational winner, sending the home supporters into a frenzy. The referee blew the final whistle shortly after, sealing a hard-fought victory for Laval and leaving Nantes with no time to recover.

On August 8, 2026 , Nantes and Red Star FC 93 went head-to-head in a pivotal Ligue 2 fixture that promised high-intensity football. Both teams entered the pitch with clear tactical instructions, setting the stage for a compelling battle under the lights. A Cagey Opening Period The match began as a tactical chess match, with both sides prioritizing defensive solidity over expansive attacking play. Red Star FC 93 established a strong physical presence early on, which led to the first booking of the game in the 26th minute when Tylel Tati was shown a yellow card for a robust challenge. Nantes attempted to dictate the tempo through possession, but they struggled to break down a well-organized away defense. As the first half progressed, the frustration of the home side became palpable. In the 36th minute, Saif-Eddine Khaoui received a yellow card as the game became increasingly fragmented by fouls. Despite several half-chances at both ends, neither goalkeeper was truly tested before the referee blew for halftime, leaving the score locked at 0-0 in a display of discipline and grit. Cabral Strikes to Break the Deadlock The second half saw both managers turn to their benches to find a breakthrough. Nantes introduced fresh legs in the form of Jovany Ikanga A Ngele and Bahereba Guirassy just before the hour mark, but it was the visitors who would find the clinical edge. In the 67th minute, Elyaz Zidane delivered a perfectly weighted assist for Kevin Cabral , who made no mistake in slotting the ball home to give Red Star FC 93 a 1-0 lead. In the final twenty minutes, the atmosphere grew increasingly hostile. Nantes pushed forward in search of an equalizer, leading to a flurry of bookings, including one for Bahmed Deuff and another for manager Michel Der Zakarian . Red Star FC 93 showed remarkable resilience to weather the storm. Despite late yellow cards for Ryad Hachem and Cheick Konate during six minutes of stoppage time, the visitors held firm to secure a massive away victory and all three points.
